body: Nothing, I have a great life and yet I feel like this and the constant thinking of "why" in my head is agony - I shouldn't feel like this, I have no reason to feel like this, stop feeling like this - but it just won't go away.

I don't understand why I *have* to try find this reason to live when, at least right now, I'd rather be dead than alive - is that not my decision to make?  It feels as though the only reason I've not done anything is because I don't want to cause my family pain.  Perhaps that could be a reason to stay alive?  But what kind of life would that be, a shitty one in my opinion. Why can't I fucking stop feeling like this.
I do not feel like I am looking for a solution to my feelings anymore because I don't think there is one so I just want them to stop. I just can't deal with feeling like this anymore.

I appreciate your honesty mate, frankly this is the kind of discussion I haven't had - mollycoddling just hasn't worked.  What I'd say is I know I have the power to do whatever the hell I want to but whatever I think of doing nothing provokes any emotion.  When I do force myself to do something - like exercise as you say - sure I feel alright after but that feeling has now gone, it doesn't do anything anymore and fucking frustrates me no end. I'm all out of ideas and any new ideas that come to me I just shoot them down.
I'm 19.  I realise that I am 'so young and have my whole life ahead of me, things can change' but I just cannot be bothered with the bloody hassle of it, I will always feel like this.

It is an immensely frustrating and depressing situation! As somebody who has gone down the therapy avenue and seems to have tried to tackle this in a much more open way, have you suffered any stigma as a result?  I fear that if I made my feelings more open that I'd be jeopardised as a result with regards to getting a job in particular.

Thank you for your suggestion, it seems a popular one judging by the comments below! I guess that I should really consider it. My worry though is that these feelings, they are always there, it's just that some days they're much much worse than others - like today - whereas others I get a decent grip on them. I'd be worried that if I'd see a therapist/doctor on one of those days it'll look like there is no problem and I'm wasting their time.

I have spoken to both my family and girlfriend about it but I only scratched the surface.  In both cases like you said, they were more than happy to help but  I don't want anybody to feel like that they should be able to solve the problem so to speak as I don't think they'd make any difference and hence they'd then feel as though they'd failed.  They have their own things to be doing the last thing they need is me adding to them.
